title: Read one value from a table or graph
subtitle: Command of Evidence · 9 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **9 of the official questions in Command of Evidence are this one** — 8 Easy, 1 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- There is a table or graph, the passage is short, and the question is literally 'According to the table/graph, what/which/when...?'.
- The choices are short: single numbers, years or category names.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the row or column the question names.
- 2) Read the cell or bar where they cross.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You read the neighbouring row, column or bar, or you choose a value that appears elsewhere in the table.
The wrong answers are real values from other rows.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You read the neighbouring row, column or bar, or you choose a value that appears elsewhere in the table.
The wrong answers are real values from other rows.
